questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: universal choking sign
questions.text: An adult at a restaurant suddenly stops eating, clutches the front of the neck with both hands, and looks panicked. AHA Part 11 calls this gesture by what name?

answers.text: The recovery position signal
The agonal gasp posture
The universal choking sign
The CPR readiness gesture

explanations.a: There is no 'recovery position signal'; the recovery position is a posture for someone breathing normally.
explanations.b: Agonal gasping is a sign of cardiac arrest, not choking.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 names the universal choking sign — clutching the neck with both hands — as the indicator that someone is choking.
explanations.d: There is no AHA-named 'CPR readiness gesture.'

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: are you choking nod
questions.text: You suspect a coworker has a foreign body airway obstruction. According to AHA Part 11, which question and response confirm severe airway obstruction?

answers.text: 'Can you walk?' — only mobility matters
'Are you OK?' — only verbal answers count
'Did you eat anything?' — if they say 'no,' it is not choking
'Are you choking?' — if the person nods 'yes' and cannot talk, severe airway obstruction is present

explanations.a: Mobility does not establish whether the airway is severely obstructed.
explanations.b: Asking 'Are you OK?' is the responsiveness check, not the FBAO confirmation question.
explanations.c: Recent eating is not the criterion for severe airway obstruction.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to ask 'Are you choking?' and confirms severe airway obstruction if the person nods 'yes' and cannot talk.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: weak or absent cough severe
questions.text: AHA Part 11's Infant FBAO algorithm lists specific signs of severe airway obstruction. Which set of findings is consistent with that algorithm?

answers.text: Loud forceful coughing and crying
Normal breathing and full conversation
Weak or absent cough, inability to cry or vocalize
Slowly developing fever and chills

explanations.a: Loud coughing indicates a mild obstruction, where the rescuer should encourage continued coughing.
explanations.b: Normal breathing and conversation rule out severe FBAO entirely.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11's Infant FBAO algorithm uses signs such as weak or absent cough and inability to cry or vocalize as evidence of severe airway obstruction.
explanations.d: Fever and chills are signs of infection, not airway obstruction.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: 5 back blows then 5 abdominal
questions.text: An adult clutches their throat, nods 'yes' to 'Are you choking?', and cannot speak. According to AHA Part 11's Adult FBAO sequence, what should you do first?

answers.text: Lay them down and start chest compressions
Give 30 forceful breaths
Give 5 forceful back blows between the shoulder blades, then 5 abdominal thrusts if needed
Wait several minutes to see if the obstruction clears on its own

explanations.a: Compressions are reserved for an unresponsive choking victim; while they are responsive, the rescuer alternates back blows and abdominal thrusts.
explanations.b: Forceful breaths during severe airway obstruction would push air past or around the obstruction inefficiently and could worsen it.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to deliver 5 forceful back blows between the shoulder blades; if those do not relieve the choking, perform 5 abdominal thrusts.
explanations.d: Waiting wastes the brief window before unconsciousness in severe airway obstruction.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: back blow technique heel of hand
questions.text: AHA Part 11 describes how to deliver back blows for choking relief in a responsive adult or child. Which technique matches?

answers.text: Use the elbow to drive into the kidney area
Use a closed fist to punch the lower back
Use the fingertips to tap gently on the upper spine
Use the heel of your hand to forcefully strike between the shoulder blades

explanations.a: Elbow strikes to the kidneys are not part of any AHA choking technique.
explanations.b: Closed-fist punches to the lower back are not part of AHA technique and may injure the kidneys.
explanations.c: Light fingertip taps will not generate the force needed to dislodge an obstruction.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 specifies using the heel of the hand to forcefully strike the person's back between their shoulder blades.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: abdominal thrust technique fist
questions.text: After 5 back blows fail to relieve choking in an adult, you proceed to abdominal thrusts. AHA Part 11 describes how to deliver them. Which technique is correct?

answers.text: Stand in front of the person and push down on the chest
Lay the person down and push laterally on the rib cage
Press both flat palms on the lower back and squeeze rhythmically
Stand behind the person, make a fist with one hand, grab it with the other, and press inward and slightly upward into the abdomen above the navel

explanations.a: Pressing on the chest from in front would be chest thrusts, not abdominal thrusts, and is reserved for special circumstances.
explanations.b: Laying the person down for lateral rib pressure is not part of choking relief in a responsive person.
explanations.c: Lateral squeezing on the back is not the AHA technique.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 describes making a fist with one hand, grabbing it with the other, and pressing inward and slightly upward into the abdomen — the classic abdominal thrust position from behind the person.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: continue alternating until expel or unresponsive
questions.text: After your first sequence of 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts in a choking adult, the obstruction is not relieved. What does AHA Part 11 direct you to do next?

answers.text: Stop and wait for EMS without further intervention
Insert your finger deep into the throat to feel for the object
Switch immediately to chest compressions while the person is still responsive
Continue alternating 5 back blows followed by 5 abdominal thrusts until the object is expelled or the person becomes unresponsive

explanations.a: Stopping leaves the obstruction unaddressed and the patient in a worsening state.
explanations.b: Blind finger sweeps are explicitly cautioned against because they may push the object farther into the airway.
explanations.c: Chest compressions are reserved for the unresponsive choking victim; while still responsive, the back-blow / abdominal-thrust sequence continues.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to continue alternating 5 back blows followed by 5 abdominal thrusts until the object is expelled or the person becomes unresponsive.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.objective: 6.3 Choking relief in special body habitus
questions.keyword: late pregnancy chest thrusts
questions.text: A visibly pregnant woman in her third trimester is choking on food. According to AHA Part 11, how should the rescuer modify the standard adult choking sequence?

answers.text: Wait until after delivery to perform any choking relief
Use only verbal coaching and never touch the person
Use 10 abdominal thrusts to overcome the resistance
Use 5 chest thrusts instead of 5 abdominal thrusts

explanations.a: Choking is acutely fatal; intervention cannot wait for delivery.
explanations.b: Verbal coaching alone fails when the obstruction is severe; physical maneuvers are required.
explanations.c: Increasing the number of abdominal thrusts does not solve the abdominal-pressure concern in late pregnancy.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 specifies that for patients in the late stages of pregnancy, 5 chest thrusts should be used instead of 5 abdominal thrusts.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.objective: 6.3 Choking relief in special body habitus
questions.keyword: cannot encircle obese chest thrusts
questions.text: You attempt abdominal thrusts on a choking adult but cannot reach around the abdomen because of body size. According to AHA Part 11, what is the correct alternative?

answers.text: Force the rescuer's arms around tighter regardless of fit
Skip the maneuver entirely
Substitute 5 chest thrusts for the 5 abdominal thrusts because the rescuer cannot encircle the abdomen
Apply pressure with the foot to the abdomen

explanations.a: Forcing a poor reach risks losing leverage and can injure both rescuer and patient.
explanations.b: Skipping intervention guarantees worsening obstruction and arrest.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 says when the rescuer is unable to encircle the patient's abdomen, 5 chest thrusts should be used instead of 5 abdominal thrusts.
explanations.d: Foot pressure is not a recognized AHA technique and would not be controllable or safe.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.objective: 6.3 Choking relief in special body habitus
questions.keyword: wheelchair patient back blows chest thrusts
questions.text: AHA Part 11 includes a section on choking relief in a responsive person in a wheelchair. Which approach is consistent with that section?

answers.text: Lift the person fully out of the chair before any maneuver
Use 5 back blows followed by 5 chest thrusts when the rescuer cannot adequately reach the abdomen
Tip the chair backward and apply pressure to the throat
Use only verbal commands and never physical maneuvers

explanations.a: Lifting the person out of the chair wastes time and may injure the rescuer or patient.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 covers responsive pregnant, obese, or wheelchair-using patients together with the principle that chest thrusts substitute for abdominal thrusts when the rescuer cannot encircle the abdomen.
explanations.c: Tipping the chair and pressing the throat are not AHA techniques and could obstruct the airway further.
explanations.d: Verbal commands alone cannot relieve a severe airway obstruction.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: no abdominal thrusts infants
questions.text: AHA Part 11 explicitly prohibits one common adult choking-relief maneuver from infants. Which is it?

answers.text: Back blows
Chest thrusts
Abdominal thrusts
Visualization for visible foreign body

explanations.a: Back blows are exactly what AHA recommends for infants — they are not prohibited.
explanations.b: Chest thrusts are part of the AHA infant choking sequence — not prohibited.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 explicitly states do not use abdominal thrusts on infants because their abdominal anatomy makes them more susceptible to internal injury.
explanations.d: Looking for a visible foreign body before removing it is part of the technique, not prohibited.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: 5 back blows 5 chest thrusts infant
questions.text: A 6-month-old responsive infant is choking. According to AHA Part 11's Infant FBAO sequence, what is the correct alternating relief sequence?

answers.text: 30 compressions and 2 breaths
5 abdominal thrusts and 5 abdominal squeezes
5 back blows alternating with 5 abdominal thrusts
5 back blows alternating with 5 chest thrusts

explanations.a: 30:2 is the CPR ratio for an unresponsive infant in cardiac arrest, not for a responsive choking infant.
explanations.b: Abdominal thrusts and abdominal squeezes are not used on infants.
explanations.c: Abdominal thrusts are explicitly prohibited for infants.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to alternate up to 5 back blows with up to 5 chest thrusts in a responsive choking infant.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: infant chest thrust heel hand sternum
questions.text: AHA Part 11 describes how to deliver chest thrusts to a choking infant. Which technique matches?

answers.text: 5 abdominal squeezes below the rib cage
5 firm pinches across the upper sternum at 5 per second
5 quick downward chest thrusts with the heel of 1 hand in the middle of the chest, on the lower half of the sternum, at about 1 per second
5 slow back-and-forth shakes by the shoulders

explanations.a: Abdominal squeezes are explicitly excluded for infants.
explanations.b: Pinching the sternum is not an AHA technique and would not generate the needed force.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11 specifies 5 quick downward chest thrusts with the heel of 1 hand in the middle of the chest, over the lower half of the sternum, at a rate of about 1 per second, each with enough force to dislodge the object.
explanations.d: Shaking an infant is dangerous and is never an AHA-recommended technique.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: continue until expel or unresponsive infant
questions.text: After your first round of 5 back blows and 5 chest thrusts in a choking infant, the object is not dislodged. What does AHA Part 11 direct you to do next?

answers.text: Repeat the sequence of up to 5 back blows and up to 5 chest thrusts until the object is removed or the infant becomes unresponsive
Stop and wait for EMS
Switch to abdominal thrusts since back blows and chest thrusts failed
Lay the infant flat and apply pressure to the throat

explanations.a: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to repeat the sequence of up to 5 back blows and up to 5 chest thrusts until actions have removed the object or the infant becomes unresponsive.
explanations.b: Stopping leaves the obstruction in place and lets the infant deteriorate.
explanations.c: Abdominal thrusts remain prohibited for infants regardless of the back-blow/chest-thrust outcome.
explanations.d: Pressure on the throat does not relieve the obstruction and can worsen it.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: infant choking activate emergency
questions.text: When you find a choking infant who is still responsive, AHA Part 11 directs you to take an immediate step in addition to starting back blows. What is it?

answers.text: Activate the emergency response system
Wait until the infant is fully unresponsive before any activation
Take the infant to a private room first
Sleep the infant on their back to relax the airway

explanations.a: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to activate the emergency response system when finding a choking infant who is still responsive.
explanations.b: Delaying activation until unresponsiveness misses the opportunity for EMS to be en route during the relief attempts.
explanations.c: Moving the infant to a private space wastes time and adds no benefit.
explanations.d: Placing the infant on their back can let the obstruction settle deeper; AHA positions the infant face-down for back blows.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: facedown head lower than chest forearm
questions.text: AHA Part 11 describes how to position a responsive choking infant for back blows. Which positioning matches?

answers.text: Hold the infant facedown with the head slightly lower than the chest, resting on your forearm
Hold the infant upright, sitting on your knee
Hold the infant face-up with the head higher than the chest
Lay the infant on the floor on their side

explanations.a: AHA Part 11 positions the infant facedown with the head slightly lower than the chest and resting on the rescuer's forearm so gravity assists in dislodging the object during back blows.
explanations.b: Upright sitting position eliminates the gravitational assist and is not the AHA-described position for back blows.
explanations.c: Face-up with head higher would work against the goal of expelling the object.
explanations.d: Side-lying on the floor is not the AHA-described position for back blows.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: support head jaw avoid throat soft tissue
questions.text: While holding a choking infant facedown for back blows, AHA Part 11 cautions against pressing on a specific anatomic region. Which region is it?

answers.text: The bony part of the chin
The soft tissue of the infant's throat
The shoulder blades
The bony part of the skull above the ears

explanations.a: Supporting the bony chin is part of correct head and jaw support — not the area to avoid.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 explicitly warns the rescuer to avoid compressing the soft tissue of the infant's throat while supporting the head and jaw.
explanations.c: Shoulder blades are the target area for back blows, not an area to avoid.
explanations.d: The skull is supported as needed during turning maneuvers; it is not the cautioned area.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: turn faceup head lower for chest thrusts
questions.text: After delivering 5 back blows to a choking infant, you turn the infant over for chest thrusts. AHA Part 11 specifies how the infant should be positioned. Which description matches?

answers.text: Hold the infant faceup with the forearm resting on the rescuer's thigh, keeping the infant's head lower than the trunk
Stand the infant up against a wall
Hold the infant facedown with the head higher than the trunk
Place the infant on the floor and step back

explanations.a: AHA Part 11 instructs the rescuer to hold the infant faceup with the forearm resting on the thigh, keeping the infant's head lower than the trunk for chest thrusts.
explanations.b: Standing the infant against a wall is not part of any AHA technique and is unsafe.
explanations.c: Facedown with head higher than the trunk is the back-blow position, not the chest-thrust position.
explanations.d: Walking away does nothing to relieve the obstruction.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: becomes unresponsive start CPR 30 compressions
questions.text: A choking adult collapses and becomes unresponsive while you are performing back blows. According to AHA Part 11, what is the correct next action?

answers.text: Continue back blows on the unresponsive person
Lower the person to the ground and start CPR with chest compressions
Tilt the head back further and try abdominal thrusts in the lying position
Wait for the person to wake up before any further care

explanations.a: Back blows on the floor on an unresponsive person are not how AHA directs the transition; CPR is the next step.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to lower the choking person who has become unresponsive to the ground and begin CPR with chest compressions because chest compressions can generate force to expel the object.
explanations.c: Repeated abdominal thrusts in a lying position are not the AHA-directed transition; CPR is the next step.
explanations.d: Waiting for the person to wake up does not happen in cardiac arrest; immediate CPR is required.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: look in mouth before each breath remove visible
questions.text: During CPR on an unresponsive choking adult, AHA Part 11 specifies what the rescuer should do each time the airway is opened to give a breath. Which action matches?

answers.text: Skip breaths entirely and only do compressions
Look in the mouth for a visible foreign object and remove it if seen — but do not perform a blind finger sweep
Insert a finger deep into the throat without looking
Press hard on the abdomen during each breath attempt

explanations.a: Compression-only CPR is not the AHA approach during a known FBAO arrest; visualization and removal of a seen object are part of the sequence.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 directs the rescuer to look in the mouth each time the airway is opened, remove a visible foreign body, but never perform a blind finger sweep.
explanations.c: Blind finger sweeps may push the object farther into the airway and are explicitly cautioned against.
explanations.d: Abdominal pressure during breaths is not part of the AHA unresponsive-choking sequence.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: no blind finger sweep
questions.text: AHA Part 11 includes an explicit caution about a finger maneuver in unresponsive choking. Which maneuver does it warn against?

answers.text: Pinching the lips shut between breaths
A blind finger sweep, because it may push the foreign body deeper into the airway
Wiping the lips with a clean cloth
Counting compressions on the rescuer's fingers

explanations.a: Closing the lips during a breath is part of mouth-to-mouth technique and is not cautioned against.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 says do not perform a blind finger sweep because it may push the foreign body back into the airway and lodge it deeper.
explanations.c: Wiping the lips is a hygiene action and is not cautioned against.
explanations.d: Counting compressions on fingers is unrelated to airway management.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: mild encourage cough
questions.text: An adult is coughing forcefully and is able to speak in short bursts after eating. According to AHA Part 11, this presentation is consistent with mild airway obstruction. What is the appropriate rescuer action?

answers.text: Encourage the person to keep coughing and monitor for worsening signs
Begin abdominal thrusts immediately
Lay the person down and start chest compressions
Insert a finger into the mouth to feel for an object

explanations.a: Mild airway obstruction is best handled by encouraging continued forceful coughing while monitoring for signs of severe obstruction.
explanations.b: Abdominal thrusts are reserved for severe airway obstruction in adults and children — not mild.
explanations.c: Compressions are for cardiac arrest or unresponsive choking, not for a coughing, talking patient.
explanations.d: Blind finger probing risks pushing a foreign body deeper.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: see medical even mild
questions.text: AHA Part 11 includes a recommendation that applies to anyone experiencing signs of mild to severe airway obstruction. Which recommendation matches?

answers.text: They should be seen by a health care professional after the event
They should be told they are fine and sent home
They should be admitted only if they lose consciousness
They should drive themselves to the hospital alone

explanations.a: AHA Part 11 says anyone experiencing signs of mild to severe airway obstruction should be seen by a health care professional, particularly after abdominal thrusts.
explanations.b: Even after relief, a medical evaluation is recommended because the obstruction may have caused complications.
explanations.c: Loss of consciousness is not the only criterion for follow-up; medical evaluation is broader.
explanations.d: Driving alone after a choking event creates safety risks and is not the AHA recommendation.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: after relief proceed unresponsive person check breathing pulse
questions.text: You successfully relieve a foreign body airway obstruction in an unresponsive adult during CPR. According to AHA Part 11, what should you do next?

answers.text: Stop all care because the person is fine now
Proceed as you would with any unresponsive person — recheck responsiveness, check breathing and pulse, confirm EMS has been activated, and provide CPR or breaths as needed
Place the person back in the choking position to verify
Administer naloxone routinely after every choking relief

explanations.a: Stopping care prematurely abandons a person who may still need CPR or breaths.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11 says after relieving choking in an unresponsive person, proceed as with any unresponsive person — recheck responsiveness, check breathing and pulse, confirm EMS activation, and provide high-quality CPR or breaths as needed.
explanations.c: There is no 'choking verification position'; the rescuer continues normal post-arrest assessment.
explanations.d: Naloxone is for opioid emergencies; routine administration after choking relief is not AHA guidance.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: universal sign choking hand to throat
questions.text: An adult at a restaurant suddenly grabs their throat with both hands while eating. According to AHA Part 11, what is this gesture?

answers.text: A signal that the person needs water
A request for the bill
The universal sign of choking — a clear indicator the rescuer should ask "Are you choking?" and prepare to act
A gesture of frustration unrelated to airway compromise

explanations.a: Hand-to-throat in distress is the universal choking sign, not a thirst gesture.
explanations.b: It is a recognized medical signal, not a service request.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11: clutching the neck with one or both hands is the universal sign of choking; the rescuer should ask "Are you choking?" and proceed to FBAO relief if confirmed.
explanations.d: In an adult who has been eating, this gesture should be presumed to indicate FBAO until proven otherwise.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: responsive adult Heimlich abdominal thrusts
questions.text: An adult is responsive but cannot speak, cough, or breathe. According to AHA Part 11, what is the correct sequence?

answers.text: Begin chest compressions immediately
Wait 2 minutes to see if the obstruction clears spontaneously before acting
Perform chest thrusts only; abdominal thrusts are not acceptable for adults
Perform abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver) — repeat until the object is expelled or the person becomes unresponsive

explanations.a: Chest compressions are for unresponsive choking patients, not responsive ones.
explanations.b: Severe FBAO is rapidly fatal; waiting will lead to deterioration.
explanations.c: Abdominal thrusts are the standard for responsive non-pregnant non-obese adults; chest thrusts are alternatives in special situations.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11: in a responsive adult with severe FBAO, perform abdominal thrusts (5 at a time per AHA, continuing until expulsion or unresponsiveness) per the FBAO algorithm.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.objective: 6.3 Choking relief in special body habitus
questions.keyword: chest thrusts obesity alternative abdominal
questions.text: A morbidly obese adult cannot speak, cough, or breathe and the rescuer cannot reach around the person's waist for abdominal thrusts. According to AHA Part 11, what is the appropriate alternative?

answers.text: Perform chest thrusts in the same manner as for a pregnant patient — placing fists on the lower sternum and thrusting inward
Perform back blows only; chest thrusts are contraindicated
Wait for EMS; rescuers cannot help with obese patients
Perform abdominal thrusts at any cost, even if the rescuer's arms cannot fully encircle

explanations.a: AHA Part 11: when abdominal thrusts cannot be performed (late pregnancy, morbid obesity, rescuer too small), chest thrusts are the recommended alternative — placed on the lower half of the sternum like compressions.
explanations.b: Back blows are part of the infant FBAO algorithm; for adults, chest thrusts are the alternative when abdominal thrusts cannot be done.
explanations.c: Withholding intervention is not the AHA recommendation; chest thrusts are the alternative.
explanations.d: Forcing abdominal thrusts when the rescuer cannot reach risks injury and is ineffective; switch to chest thrusts.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: infant FBAO 5 back blows 5 chest thrusts
questions.text: A 9-month-old has signs of severe FBAO (weak/absent cough, no cry, color change). According to AHA Part 11 infant FBAO algorithm, what is the immediate sequence?

answers.text: Perform abdominal thrusts as for an adult
Deliver 5 back blows followed by 5 chest thrusts; repeat until the object is expelled or the infant becomes unresponsive
Perform chest compressions immediately as for unresponsive arrest
Hold the infant upside-down by the ankles and shake

explanations.a: Abdominal thrusts are not used in infants under 1 year because of injury risk to abdominal organs.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11: alternate 5 back blows (infant facedown, head lower than trunk, on the rescuer's forearm) and 5 chest thrusts (infant faceup, head lower than trunk, two fingers on lower sternum) until expulsion or unresponsiveness.
explanations.c: Chest compressions begin only if the infant becomes unresponsive.
explanations.d: Inverted shaking can cause serious injury and is not part of the algorithm.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: infant back blow position facedown forearm
questions.text: A rescuer is preparing to deliver back blows to an infant with severe FBAO. According to AHA Part 11, what is the correct position?

answers.text: Hold the infant upright with the head higher than the trunk
Lay the infant on a flat hard surface with the head turned to the side
Hold the infant facedown along the rescuer's forearm, supporting the head and jaw, with the head lower than the trunk; rest the forearm on the rescuer's thigh for additional support
Hold the infant by both ankles inverted in mid-air

explanations.a: Head-up position works against gravity and reduces effectiveness.
explanations.b: Back blows require active rescuer support, not a flat surface position.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11: facedown along the forearm, head lower than the trunk, jaw and head supported, forearm on the thigh — this uses gravity to help dislodge the object during back blows.
explanations.d: Inverted ankle holding is dangerous and not part of the algorithm.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: unresponsive choking begin CPR no blind sweep
questions.text: An adult choking patient becomes unresponsive after several rounds of abdominal thrusts. According to AHA Part 11, what is the next action?

answers.text: Continue abdominal thrusts on the unresponsive patient until the object is expelled
Perform a blind finger sweep deep into the throat
Wait for EMS to arrive

Lower the patient to the ground, activate emergency response if not already done, and begin CPR — when opening the airway to give breaths, look in the mouth and remove any visible foreign body, but do NOT do blind finger sweeps

explanations.a: Abdominal thrusts are not performed on unresponsive patients; CPR is initiated.
explanations.b: Blind finger sweeps risk pushing the object deeper and are not recommended.
explanations.c: CPR begins immediately; waiting reduces survival.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11: when a choking patient becomes unresponsive, lower them safely, ensure EMS is activated, begin CPR; remove only visible objects when opening the airway, never sweep blindly.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: CPR after FBAO look remove visible object
questions.text: During CPR on a patient who became unresponsive while choking, the rescuer prepares to deliver breaths. According to AHA Part 11, what additional step is performed before each breath that is NOT done in standard CPR?

answers.text: Open the mouth and look for a foreign body before each rescue breath; remove only what is visible
Compress the abdomen with each breath as a substitute for abdominal thrusts
Check carotid pulse with each breath
Sweep deep into the throat with a finger before each breath

explanations.a: AHA Part 11: in CPR after FBAO collapse, look in the mouth before each breath and remove any visible foreign body — this differs from standard CPR where this look-and-remove is not part of the cycle.
explanations.b: Combining abdominal compressions with breaths is not part of any AHA algorithm.
explanations.c: Pulse checks are limited to ≤10 seconds and not synchronized with breaths.
explanations.d: Blind sweeps are explicitly contraindicated; only visible objects are removed.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: mild FBAO effective cough monitor
questions.text: An adult with a partial airway obstruction is forcefully coughing and able to speak in short phrases. According to AHA Part 11, what is the correct rescuer action?

answers.text: Perform abdominal thrusts immediately
Encourage the patient to keep coughing, stay nearby, monitor, and only intervene if the cough becomes weak or stops, the patient cannot speak, or color/consciousness changes
Lay the patient down and begin CPR
Immediately give 5 back blows even if the cough is effective

explanations.a: Abdominal thrusts are reserved for severe FBAO with weak/absent cough — interrupting an effective cough may worsen the obstruction.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11: a forceful cough is more effective than any rescuer maneuver; encourage continued coughing and monitor for deterioration.
explanations.c: CPR is for unresponsive patients in arrest, not coughing patients.
explanations.d: Back blows are for severe FBAO, not effective coughs.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: severe FBAO weak cough cyanosis stridor
questions.text: During FBAO assessment, AHA Part 11 distinguishes between mild and severe airway obstruction. Which set of findings indicates SEVERE obstruction in an adult?

answers.text: Loud, forceful cough; able to speak in full sentences; pink color
Mild wheezing while still talking comfortably
Weak or no cough; high-pitched stridor or no air movement; inability to speak; cyanosis or rapid color change
Coughing while continuing to chew the food

explanations.a: Loud cough and full sentences indicate mild (effective) obstruction.
explanations.b: Mild wheezing with normal speech indicates partial, not severe, obstruction.
explanations.c: AHA Part 11: severe obstruction = weak/absent cough, no/poor air movement, inability to speak, cyanosis — the rescuer must intervene immediately.
explanations.d: Continued chewing/coughing indicates a still-functional airway.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: after choking medical evaluation injury assessment
questions.text: A choking adult expels the foreign body after abdominal thrusts and is now coughing and breathing. According to AHA Part 11, what should the rescuer do next?

answers.text: Send the person home immediately
Repeat 5 abdominal thrusts as a "safety" precaution
Force fluids by mouth to clear residual material

Recommend medical evaluation, even if the person feels well, because internal injury (rib fracture, abdominal trauma, aspirated material) may need assessment, and observe for any signs of deterioration

explanations.a: Sending home without evaluation misses internal injuries from the thrusts and possible aspiration.
explanations.b: Repeating thrusts after the obstruction is cleared causes injury without benefit.
explanations.c: Forcing fluids may cause aspiration in someone whose airway has just been compromised.
explanations.d: AHA Part 11: thrust-related injuries (rib fractures, splenic/liver injury) and aspiration can cause delayed problems; medical evaluation is recommended even if the person feels normal.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: pregnancy after choking obstetric evaluation
questions.text: A choking patient was relieved by chest thrusts during pregnancy. The patient now feels fine. According to AHA Part 11 and obstetric guidance, what is the appropriate follow-up?

answers.text: Recommend prompt obstetric evaluation in addition to standard medical evaluation, because chest thrusts on a pregnant patient can affect both maternal and fetal status (placental abruption, fetal distress) even when the patient feels well
No follow-up is needed because the obstruction was cleared
Cancel any obstetric appointments because the situation is resolved
Continue normal activity without any healthcare contact

explanations.a: Pregnancy after chest thrusts requires a higher threshold for evaluation due to maternal and fetal risks.
explanations.b: Symptom resolution does not exclude internal or fetal injury.
explanations.c: Cancelling obstetric care after a thoracic-trauma incident is the opposite of appropriate follow-up.
explanations.d: Even an asymptomatic pregnant patient should be evaluated after a chest-thrust intervention.

questions.name: Choking and Airway Obstruction
questions.keyword: child after FBAO aspiration injury evaluation
questions.text: A child was relieved of FBAO after back blows and chest thrusts. The child is now breathing normally. According to AHA Part 11, why should the child still be evaluated by a healthcare professional?

answers.text: Children always need follow-up regardless of any event
Pieces of the foreign body may have moved into the lower airway, and chest thrusts can cause rib fracture or organ injury — both may be silent initially and need professional evaluation
Schools require a doctor's note after every choking event
The rescuer wants documentation for legal reasons

explanations.a: Routine universal pediatric follow-up is not the rationale; specific risks justify the recommendation.
explanations.b: AHA Part 11: residual aspirated material can cause delayed pneumonitis or atelectasis, and thrust-related thoracic/abdominal injury can be silent — evaluation is recommended after any FBAO requiring intervention.
explanations.c: School documentation policy is administrative, not the medical rationale.
explanations.d: Liability documentation is not the AHA reason for medical evaluation.
